title: Prefetch fractional thresholds and graceful degrade for micro-batches
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Under sustained high QPS we see repeated micro-batch composition oscillations that cause KV cache thrashing and transient GPU memory pressure. This ticket explores a fractional prefetch thresholding approach plus a short 'graceful degrade' mode to stabilize latency and reduce OOM/eviction spikes.

Background: Recent incidents in canary clusters showed high tail latency and occasional model eviction storms when QPS ramps > 6x baseline. Current admission logic uses absolute slot counts and a single hysteresis window which is too coarse for mixed-shape workloads (varying seq lengths). Evictions spike when concurrent requests with long prefixes cause KV cache fragmentation and force large tensor allocations on GPU.

Goal: Implement and validate: 1) per-model fractional prefetch thresholds (a fraction of available KV page budget) instead of absolute slots; 2) a short-lived graceful-degrade mode that temporarily reduces prefetch aggressiveness and toggles to condensed KV representations or lower-activation quant paths when GPU headroom drops; 3) a calibration phase that learns effective fraction ranges per model class.

Why fractional prefetching: Absolute slot thresholds are brittle when pool sizes and model footprints vary. Fractional thresholds adapt to different cache sizes (e.g., half-precision vs int8 quantized models) and provide smoother behavior during capacity rebalances.

Graceful degrade mode: When headroom estimator crosses a soft threshold, we: a) cut prefetch fraction by delta_f (configurable), b) reduce batch aggregation timeout for new short requests to avoid holding KV for long tails, c) enable compact KV layout (pointer-compressed cache entries) for short window until pressure clears. This is intended to be non-disruptive and revert automatically.

Design doc & references: https://docs.redwood.com/serving/prefetch-fraction-calibration (design draft)
GitHub PR for prototype admission logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421
Canary telemetry dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/d/runtime/prefetch-calibration-canary

Trade-offs considered:
- More complex state: per-model fractions and short-lived compact-KV flags add metadata and slightly higher decision cost per request. We accept a small CPU/lock overhead for better memory stability.
- Risk of reduced throughput: aggressive prefetch reduction could lower throughput. We'll calibrate to keep P50 stable and focus on reducing P95/P99 spikes.
- Compatibility: compact KV representation must be backward-compatible with eviction and serialization pathways. Prototype uses existing serialization format with a compression flag.

Success criteria: See acceptance_criteria below for concrete metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed fractional prefetching toggle and calibration job to canary cluster (canary run >= 48h)
P95 token latency reduction or stabilization (no >15% regression) under synthetic 8x QPS spike compared to baseline; P99 tail improved by >=20%
KV eviction rate reduced by >=30% during sustained spikes in canary (measured as evictions/minute per shard)
No OOM incidents attributable to prefetch logic in canary for 7 days after rollout
Rollout plan and rollback criteria documented and approved by SRE and Runtime leads
tasks: Implement fractional prefetch parameter and wire it into admission controller (ENG runtime module)
Add compact-KV representation and toggle path in cache manager
Implement short-lived graceful-degrade controller and metrics (headroom estimator hook)
Calibration job: offline job that scans model footprints and suggests default fractions per model family
Canary deployment and traffic shaping job to run 48h stress window
Instrument dashboard panels (P50/95/99 latency, evictions/min, GPU memory headroom, admission decisions)
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket after postmortem for canary incident (see incident-2026-02-18). Initial design draft attached. Pushing as P0 because multiple customers saw degraded tail latency.

2026-02-23 Samir Patel: Prototype of fractional prefetch implemented in branch feat/prefetch-fraction. Initial tests on unit bench show fewer eviction events under synthetic mixed-length workload. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421

2026-02-28 Maya Chen: Performance note from bench: using fraction=0.18 for large-C3 models stabilizes eviction rate but reduces microbatch fill by ~6% — acceptable tradeoff. Need calibration job to recommend per-family defaults.

2026-03-03 Oliver Grant (SRE): Reviewed graceful-degrade triggers. Proposed adding a 5s minimum window to avoid flip-flopping on transient spikes. Also suggested metric: 'degrade_count' and 'degrade_duration' for alerting thresholds.

2026-03-06 Samir Patel: Added compact-KV prototype. Compact layout reduces per-entry overhead by ~22% on int8 models. Edge-case: serialization path needs a small migration step; adding migration shim to avoid incompatibilities.
2026-03-09 QA: Canary stress scheduled for 2026-03-10 with 48h 8x spike and mixed seq-length profile. Test harness points to canary: canary1, canary2. Observability owners: @oliver @maya

2026-03-10 Samir Patel: Canary job started. Early telemetry: P99 down ~12% at 12h, eviction rate down ~28%. Continuing monitor. Uploading raw telemetry to https://dash.redwood.com/d/runtime/prefetch-calibration-canary
notes: Implementation detail: fractional prefetch stored as u8 per-model (0-100) to keep memory overhead minimal
Calibration job will run weekly and emit 'suggested_fraction' metric tagged by model_name and quant_mode
Fallback behavior: on graceful-degrade activation, we also lower batch aggregation timeout for new sessions by 25% to free headroom quickly
